analysis: This batch contains only documentation and a changelog: changelog.d/ssd-restore-without-eval-lock.md (new, lines 1-10) and docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 252-259). No source code is supplied. The docs describe a behavior change in SSD complete-checkpoint restore. Provider-staged imports now create destinations already available from host bytes and never evaluate or fence them, so staging does not wait on MLX's process-wide evalLock while another request's prefill chunk runs. The code (CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift) and the destination contract in ../reference/ssd-kv-cache.md are not in the supplied evidence, so none of this was verified. Relevant threats: T-041 (SSD prefix cache, TTFT oracle, at-rest artifacts), T-028 (residual GPU/host memory), A-001. Questions for integration or deeper review of the code: (1) Restore faster under contention could change the TTFT timing oracle only within the already-accepted SEC-035 same-account scope; cache-hit latency likely becomes less contended-dependent. (2) Does skipping eval/fence leave plaintext KV host bytes in host buffers longer, or leave the lifetime of the host Data uncontrolled until lazy materialization? That would be a T-028/T-014 memory-residency matter. (3) Does lazy 'available from host bytes' preserve the GCM authentication, AAD binding, and salt scoping checks before destination creation? Those are in unchanged code and cannot be assessed here. No security-relevant regression is established from docs alone. The mitigations in T-041 (HMAC names, TTL, KEK, AAD) are not described as altered.
